title: Fit a tactile sensor pad on a gripper fingertip while holding the finger's holder
instruction: Fit the tactile sensor pad onto the spare gripper finger standing in the orange holder. The pad goes on the finger's top face, over the two small holes near the fingertip, the end with the red band. Pick the pad up from the black tray, keep its grey rubber face up, turn it so its amber cable tab points along the finger, away from the fingertip, and set its two pins into the holes. Then press it down firmly until it sits flat on the finger. Pressed on its own, the holder tips over the edge of its head: hold the holder down by the block at its left end with one hand while you press with the other, and do not slide it away. Let go once the pad is on.
context: Tactile sensing labs fit and replace sensor pads on robot fingertips all the time; a pad on the wrong way round or not fully home gives a skewed or dead signal. Robots that can do this can help build and maintain other robots.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. Finger in its holder, one loose body, 90 g. Finger: an aluminium bar 60 x 20 x 10 mm lying along y (x 0.29 to 0.31, y -0.111 to -0.051), gripping face up, its underside 4 cm and its face 5 cm above the table. Its fingertip end, at y = -0.111, has a red band 1.5 mm wide across the face. In the face, two square locating holes 3.4 mm across and 4.5 mm deep, centred at (0.30, -0.105) and (0.30, -0.095); a black plate shows at the bottom of each. Holder: orange PLA, 32 mm wide (x 0.284 to 0.316): a head 3 cm long and 5 cm tall (y -0.066 to -0.036) with a slot the finger's root sits in for 15 mm, so the finger sticks out 45 mm past the head to the right, in the air; a flat foot 8 mm thick (y -0.036 to 0.104); and a block 3 cm long and 3.4 cm tall at its left end (y 0.104 to 0.134). Tray, fixed: black anti-static plastic, a plate 50 x 50 x 4 mm centred at (0.22, -0.20) with a post 14 mm along x, 10 mm along y and 12 mm tall in its middle, its top 16 mm above the table, and a channel 3.4 mm wide and 4.5 mm deep along x across the post's top, open at both ends. Tactile pad, loose, 4 g: a green rigid circuit board 18 x 18 x 3 mm with a grey silicone rubber face 18 x 18 x 3 mm on top, 6 mm thick in all; two steel locating pins 2 mm across and 3.5 mm long under it, 10 mm apart, either side of its centre; and a flat amber polyimide cable tab 10 mm wide, 8 mm long and 0.5 mm thick sticking out from the middle of one edge, in line with the pins, 1 mm above the underside. It sits centred on the post, rubber face up, pins down in the channel, its tab pointing along +x, away from the robots, its edges overhanging the post by 2 to 4 mm. No other objects.
scoring: Measured once everything has come to rest, relative to the finger. The pad is in the holes if its centre is within 1 mm of the point midway between the holes, it is tilted no more than 10 degrees from the face, and its underside is no more than 3 mm above the face and no more than 1 mm below it. It is seated if its underside is within 0.5 mm of the face. 0 if the pad is not in the holes. 0.25 if it is in the holes but not seated. Seated: 1.0 if the tab points within 20 degrees of along the finger, away from the fingertip; 0.5 otherwise. The pins only go in with the tab along the finger, so 0.5 in practice means the tab turned towards the fingertip. In a real trial, check the gap under the pad's edges with a 0.5 mm feeler gauge and photograph the finger from above for the tab's direction.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Pull the pad off and set it back centred on the tray's post, rubber up, pins in the channel, tab pointing away from the robots; set the holder back at its start with its foot flat. In simulation the press fit is restored at each reset. A real pin fit loosens over many cycles: replace the pad or the finger when it no longer takes about 4 N to press home.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at 240 Hz. Finger and holder are one body of uniform density. The pins are plain 2 mm pins in 3.4 mm square holes. The press fit is a sprung plate under the holes that holds the pad 2 mm up and gives at 4 N, then lets it drop onto the face. The rubber face is rigid, the cable tab is a stiff 0.5 mm plate with no cable, and no sensor signal is simulated.
